subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should Docker multi-instance operation remain documented manual Compose/profile workflow for now?
rationale: The request creates new official operator UX and lifecycle semantics across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose names, update/delete behavior, and sandbox boundaries; source inspection shows no existing narrow implementation to clean up automatically.

options.title: Sponsor a core lifecycle
options.body: Approve a minimal explicit core design for named Docker instances before implementation, including identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Leave the issue open as a design backlog item while relying on current multi-gateway docs, env variables, Docker setup script, and ClawDock helpers.

options.title: Route to wrapper first
options.body: Decline core ownership unless a missing core API is identified, and ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or ClawHub package around the current primitives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a minimal explicit core design for named Docker instances before implementation, including identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest feature history points to profile/multi-gateway docs and setup product direction owned or introduced by steipete.
